views.name: ball_event_with_players
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.team_batting,
  b.team_bowling,
  b.striker_batting_position,
  b.striker,
  striker_player.player_name AS striker_player_name,
  b.non_striker,
  non_striker_player.player_name AS non_striker_player_name,
  b.bowler,
  bowler_player.player_name AS bowler_player_name,
  m.match_date,
  m.season_id,
  m.venue,
  m.team_1,
  m.team_2,
  m.toss_winner,
  m.toss_decision,
  m.match_winner
FROM ball_by_ball b
LEFT JOIN player striker_player ON b.striker = striker_player.player_id
LEFT JOIN player non_striker_player ON b.non_striker = non_striker_player.player_id
LEFT JOIN player bowler_player ON b.bowler = bowler_player.player_id
LEFT JOIN match m ON b.match_id = m.match_id

params.description: Row-level ball-by-ball view enriched with player and match attributes for each delivery (grain: match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve detailed information about a specific delivery (who batted, bowled, player names, and match context). | Compose additional per-ball metrics (e.g., runs, extras, wicket flags) by joining to other ball-level fact views. | Aggregate to over/innings/match level while preserving player and match context at delivery granularity. | Filter deliveries by player, team, venue, season, or match attributes before further aggregation.
params.output_schema: match_id: match identifier — derived from ball_by_ball.match_id | innings_no: innings number within the match — derived from ball_by_ball.innings_no | over_id: over identifier within the innings — derived from ball_by_ball.over_id | ball_id: ball identifier within the over — derived from ball_by_ball.ball_id | team_batting: team currently batting on this delivery — derived from ball_by_ball.team_batting | team_bowling: team bowling on this delivery — derived from ball_by_ball.team_bowling | striker_batting_position: batting position of the striker at this delivery (source column) — derived from ball_by_ball.striker_batting_position | striker: player_id of the striker batter on this delivery — derived from ball_by_ball.striker | striker_player_name: player_name for the striker — derived from player.player_name (joined as striker_player) matched by ball_by_ball.striker = player.player_id | non_striker: player_id of the non-striker batter on this delivery — derived from ball_by_ball.non_striker | non_striker_player_name: player_name for the non-striker — derived from player.player_name (joined as non_striker_player) matched by ball_by_ball.non_striker = player.player_id | bowler: player_id of the bowler on this delivery — derived from ball_by_ball.bowler | bowler_player_name: player_name for the bowler — derived from player.player_name (joined as bowler_player) matched by ball_by_ball.bowler = player.player_id | match_date: date of the match — derived from match.match_date (joined by ball_by_ball.match_id = match.match_id) | season_id: season identifier for the match — derived from match.season_id | venue: match venue — derived from match.venue | team_1: team_1 from match record — derived from match.team_1 | team_2: team_2 from match record — derived from match.team_2 | toss_winner: toss winner for the match — derived from match.toss_winner | toss_decision: toss decision for the match — derived from match.toss_decision | match_winner: match winning team — derived from match.match_winner
params.grounded_columns: ball_by_ball.match_id | ball_by_ball.innings_no | ball_by_ball.over_id | ball_by_ball.ball_id | ball_by_ball.team_batting | ball_by_ball.team_bowling | ball_by_ball.striker_batting_position | ball_by_ball.striker | ball_by_ball.non_striker | ball_by_ball.bowler | player.player_id | player.player_name | match.match_id | match.match_date | match.season_id | match.venue | match.team_1 | match.team_2 | match.toss_winner | match.toss_decision | match.match_winner
params.metric: This view exposes no aggregated measures at its own grain — all columns are sourced attributes. If you create derived metrics, define them explicitly after joining (examples): | deliveries_count = COUNT(*) over desired grouping (explicit aggregation; not computed in view) | unique_bowlers_count = COUNT(DISTINCT bowler) over grouping (explicit aggregation) | Note: do not assume precomputed aggregates exist in this view; it is a 1:1 row per ball fact enrichment.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension-like tables or one-row-per-entity views on their natural keys — safe because they do not multiply this view's rows. | Safe joins (do NOT duplicate measures): | - join to match_summary_basic on match_id — safe because match_summary_basic is one-row-per-match (no duplication of ball rows). | - join to player_match_roster on (match_id, player_id) but only when roster is one-row-per-player-per-match (ensure its grain is player+match); if roster is one-row-per-player-per-match it is safe for player-level enrichment. | Do NOT join without care (these will multiply rows/measures unless you aggregate first): | - do NOT join directly to one-to-many ball-level fact views such as extras_per_ball_with_type, batsman_runs_per_ball, or wickets_with_kind_and_player without ensuring you preserve or re-aggregate cardinality — these are also ball-grain and may be one-to-many per ball (e.g., multiple extra types, multiple wicket events) and will duplicate this view's row-level semantics. | - do NOT join to player_match_roster or other roster views if they are one-to-many (e.g., multiple role rows per player per match) without reducing to one row per (match_id, player_id). | Recommended safe composition patterns: | - To aggregate measures per-match/over/innings: aggregate this view (GROUP BY match_id[, innings_no[, over_id]]) then join to other aggregated datasets. | - To add ball-level metrics provided by sibling ball-grain views (batsman_runs_per_ball, extras_per_ball_with_type, wickets_with_kind_and_player): join on (match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id) only when those sibling views are known to be strictly one-row-per-ball or when you plan to re-aggregate after join. If the sibling view is one-row-per-ball, the join is 1:1 and safe; if it is one-to-many, aggregate sibling first (e.g., SUM/ranking) to avoid multiplication. | - To enrich player attributes for a particular role (striker/non_striker/bowler): this view already left-joins player names by player_id. If you need additional player-level attributes from player or player-match tables, join on player_id for the specific role and ensure the player-side is one-row-per-player (or pre-aggregated to one row per player). | Practical keys to use for joins: | - Ball-level joins: (match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id) — use only with other views/tables that are one-row-per-ball or aggregated to ball-level. | - Match-level joins: match_id — use with one-row-per-match tables/views. | - Player-level joins: player_id (and match_id if using player-match scoped data) — ensure the right grain (player vs player+match).

views.description: Denormalized ball-level events joined with participating player and match metadata. Use this when answering questions that need per-ball context including which players (striker, non_striker, bowler), teams, and match-level attributes. | Use for: List ball-by-ball events with player names for a match/season/venue; Aggregate runs/wickets by bowler or batsman using ball-level joins; Filter balls by team batting or bowling and compute counts
validated_on: For each IPL season, identify the top three batsmen with the highest total runs scored and the top three bowlers with the most wickets taken, excluding ‘run out’, ‘hit wicket’, and ‘retired hurt’ dismissals. In the event of ties in runs or wickets, break the tie using the smaller player ID. Then output these six players in matched positions—batsman 1 with bowler 1, batsman 2 with bowler 2, and batsman 3 with bowler 3—in ascending order of the season ID, along with each player’s total runs or wickets.

views.name: batsman_runs_per_ball
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.striker,
  p.player_name AS striker_player_name,
  bs.runs_scored
FROM batsman_scored bs
JOIN ball_by_ball b ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
LEFT JOIN player p ON b.striker = p.player_id

params.description: Per-ball batsman scoring: one row per ball indicating the striker and runs scored by that batsman on that ball.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve the batsman and runs scored for each individual legal delivery (ball) in a match/innings/over. | Compute further aggregations by composing per-ball runs into per-over, per-innings or per-player metrics (after appropriate aggregation). | Join ball-level player metadata (e.g., striker name) to ball-level events or stats.
params.output_schema: match_id: match identifier — derived from ball_by_ball.match_id | innings_no: innings number within the match — derived from ball_by_ball.innings_no | over_id: over identifier within the innings — derived from ball_by_ball.over_id | ball_id: ball identifier within the over — derived from ball_by_ball.ball_id | striker: player_id of the batsman on strike for that ball — derived from ball_by_ball.striker | striker_player_name: player_name corresponding to striker — derived from player.player_name (LEFT JOIN on player.player_id) | runs_scored: runs scored by the batsman on that ball — derived from batsman_scored.runs_scored
params.grounded_columns: batsman_scored.match_id | batsman_scored.innings_no | batsman_scored.over_id | batsman_scored.ball_id | batsman_scored.runs_scored | ball_by_ball.match_id | ball_by_ball.innings_no | ball_by_ball.over_id | ball_by_ball.ball_id | ball_by_ball.striker | player.player_id | player.player_name
params.metric: runs_scored = batsman_scored.runs_scored (atomic, per-row metric; NOT an aggregate in this view)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensional/look-up views/tables one-to-one with this view's grain without aggregating — safe examples: |  - Join to player_match_roster on (striker = player_id AND match_id) — safe because player_match_roster is expected to be at most one row per player per match, so it will not duplicate runs_scored. |  - Join to player (or any player-level one-row-per-player table) on (striker = player_id) — safe because player is one-row-per-player and does not duplicate ball-level measures. |  - Join to match_summary_basic on (match_id) — safe because match_summary_basic is one-row-per-match and will not multiply ball rows. |  | Do NOT directly join this view to one-to-many tables/views that expand rows per ball (without re-aggregation) because they will multiply runs_scored and other per-ball measures. Examples to avoid or to use only after aggregation: |  - Do NOT join directly to extras_per_ball_with_type (if that view can contain multiple extra rows per ball) unless you first aggregate extras to ball-level; otherwise runs_scored may be duplicated. |  - Do NOT join directly to ball_event_with_players if that view contains multiple event rows per ball (e.g., multiple events recorded for the same ball) without ensuring event-level deduplication or aggregation to the same grain (match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id). |  - Do NOT join directly to wickets_with_kind_and_player without confirming it is at most one row per ball; if wickets_with_kind_and_player can contain multiple rows per ball (e.g., multiple wicket records), aggregate or deduplicate to ball-level first. |  | Guidance for composing aggregations: |  - To compute per-player or per-match aggregates from this view, first aggregate runs_scored at the desired grouping (e.g., SUM(runs_scored) GROUP BY match_id, striker) before joining to any one-to-many detail tables. |  - When composing into higher-level aggregates (over-level, innings-level), group by the target grain (for example, GROUP BY match_id, innings_no, over_id to get runs per over) so that further joins to one-to-many tables do not multiply measures. |  | Reasoning about join-safe cardinality: this view has deterministic one-row-per base ball identified by the grain (match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id) because it selects rows from batsman_scored joined to ball_by_ball on the same ball keys. As long as you join other datasets that are one-row-per-(match/ball) or one-row-per-player (when joining on striker) the per-ball atomic measure runs_scored will remain unduplicated. Any join that can introduce multiple rows for the same ball MUST be preceded by aggregation or de-duplication to the ball-level grain.

views.description: Ball-level pairing of batsman runs with ball event (to know which batsman scored on which ball). Useful for aggregations of batsman runs, strike-rate, and per-innings scoring. | Use for: Total runs by a batsman in a match/season/career; Balls where a batsman scored X runs; Strike-rate and scoring breakdown per batsman

views.name: wickets_with_kind_and_player
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  w.match_id,
  w.innings_no,
  w.over_id,
  w.ball_id,
  w.player_out,
  p.player_name AS player_out_name,
  w.kind_out
FROM wicket_taken w
LEFT JOIN player p ON w.player_out = p.player_id

params.description: Provides wicket events per ball with the dismissed player id, their name, and dismissal kind — one row per wicket-taking ball (grained by match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id).
params.when_to_use: List all wickets in a match/innings/over/ball with player identity and dismissal kind | Join wicket-level details into broader ball-level analyses without duplicating wicket attributes | Compose player-level wicket aggregations by aggregating this view (e.g., count wickets per player per match) | Enrich ball-level event streams with the dismissed batter's name and dismissal kind
params.output_schema: match_id: match identifier — derived from wicket_taken.match_id | innings_no: innings number within the match — derived from wicket_taken.innings_no | over_id: over identifier within the innings — derived from wicket_taken.over_id | ball_id: ball identifier within the over — derived from wicket_taken.ball_id | player_out: player_id of the dismissed player — derived from wicket_taken.player_out | player_out_name: player_name of the dismissed player — derived from player.player_name (via LEFT JOIN on wicket_taken.player_out = player.player_id) | kind_out: textual code/type describing dismissal kind (e.g., 'bowled', 'caught') — derived from wicket_taken.kind_out
params.grounded_columns: wicket_taken.match_id | wicket_taken.innings_no | wicket_taken.over_id | wicket_taken.ball_id | wicket_taken.player_out | wicket_taken.kind_out | player.player_id | player.player_name
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are computed in this view; all columns are raw/passthrough from base tables. | If used as source for metrics: wicket_count = COUNT(*) when grouping by desired keys (e.g., player_out, match_id)
params.composition: Safe to join (one-to-one or many-to-one from this view's perspective): join to match_summary_basic on match_id — safe because match_summary_basic is one-row-per-match, so it will not duplicate wicket rows. | Safe to join: join to player_match_roster on (match_id, player_id = player_out) — safe when player_match_roster is one-row-per-player-per-match (it enriches wicket rows without duplicating wicket measures). | Unsafe to join without re-aggregation: do NOT directly join to ball_event_with_players, batsman_runs_per_ball, extras_per_ball_with_type, or any other ball-level one-to-many view/table on (match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id) unless you intend to expand wicket rows — these are one-to-many relative to a single wicket row (for example, a ball may have multiple related events or extras) and will multiply counts if you treat wicket rows as atomic measures. | Unsafe to join without aggregation: do NOT join to wickets_agg_per_player_match or batsman_runs_agg_per_player_match on player/match keys expecting no duplication — those are aggregated summaries; if joined you should join on matching grain and be explicit whether you want per-wicket detail combined with per-player aggregates (prefer joining aggregated view on player+match keys where aggregated rows are one-per-player-per-match). | Guidance for building aggregations on top: when aggregating this view (e.g., COUNT(*) AS wickets_per_player_per_match GROUP BY match_id, player_out), you can safely join other one-row-per-player-per-match dimensions (player_match_roster) or one-row-per-match dimensions (match_summary_basic) afterwards without changing the aggregate semantics. If you need to join ball-level one-to-many detail to compute derived metrics, first aggregate that detail to the same grain as this view (match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id) or to the target aggregation grain to avoid row multiplication.

views.description: One row per wicket event including dismissed player name and basic match context. Use for per-player dismissal counts, types of dismissals, and timeline of wickets in an innings. | Use for: Count dismissals by player or by kind; Sequence of wickets in an innings or match; Which players were out and how in a match

views.name: extras_per_ball_with_type
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.match_id,
  e.innings_no,
  e.over_id,
  e.ball_id,
  e.extra_type,
  e.extra_runs
FROM extra_runs e

params.description: Provides one row per ball that had extra runs, listing the match, innings, over, ball identifiers, the extra type and the number of extra runs.
params.when_to_use: List or filter individual deliveries that contained extras (e.g., find all wides, no-balls, byes, leg-byes). | Compute ball-level statistics involving extras (e.g., join with ball-level events to show players involved on balls with extras). | Compose aggregated extra-run summaries by grouping these ball-level extra rows (e.g., total extra runs per match/innings/type). | Filter deliveries with extras before joining to other per-ball views (e.g., to limit further analysis to only extra deliveries).
params.output_schema: match_id: match identifier; derived from base column extra_runs.match_id | innings_no: innings number within the match; derived from base column extra_runs.innings_no | over_id: over identifier within the innings; derived from base column extra_runs.over_id | ball_id: ball identifier within the over; derived from base column extra_runs.ball_id | extra_type: categorical type of the extra (e.g., wide, noball, bye, legbye); derived from base column extra_runs.extra_type | extra_runs: number of runs awarded as extras on this ball; derived from base column extra_runs.extra_runs
params.grounded_columns: extra_runs.match_id | extra_runs.innings_no | extra_runs.over_id | extra_runs.ball_id | extra_runs.extra_type | extra_runs.extra_runs
params.metric: extra_runs = extra_runs.extra_runs  -- atomic numeric value per row (ball-level); not an aggregate in this view
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match_summary_basic on match_id — safe because match_summary_basic is one-row-per-match, so it will not duplicate per-ball rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_match_roster on (match_id) and optionally player_id if filtering by player to add player-level metadata — safe only when you constrain roster to one row per player-match; joining roster without player filter may expand roster per match (one-to-many) and thus multiply rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to ball_event_with_players on (match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id) — safe because ball_event_with_players is a per-ball normalized/joined view (one row per ball event) so it will align 1:1 with this view's ball grain and not duplicate extra_runs. | DO NOT join directly to one-to-many aggregations (e.g., batsman_runs_agg_per_player_match, wickets_agg_per_player_match) without re-aggregation or proper grouping first — those are aggregated at player-match grain and can create many-to-one relationships that duplicate this view's ball rows unless you aggregate the joined side back to the ball or to the same grain. | DO NOT join to raw event tables or views that are one-to-many at the ball grain (for example a hypothetical ball_events_with_multiple_actions per ball) unless you first aggregate those events to the ball-level, because joining a one-to-many child to this per-ball view will multiply extra_runs occurrences. | When composing higher-level metrics (e.g., total extras per match or per innings), aggregate extra_runs after selecting/joining: SELECT match_id, SUM(extra_runs) FROM extras_per_ball_with_type GROUP BY match_id — avoid summing after joining to tables that expand rows without re-aggregation. | If you need player-level attribution (e.g., which bowler conceded an extra), join ball_event_with_players (1:1 at ball grain) first to attach the player_id, then aggregate by player_id so measures remain correct and not duplicated.

views.description: One row per ball extra runs event joined with ball identity and match/innings. Use to analyze extras by type, totals conceded by innings, or to attach extras to balls for total-run calculations. | Use for: Aggregate extras by type per match/innings/season; Compute total extras conceded by a team in an innings

views.name: player_match_roster
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.match_id,
  pm.player_id,
  p.player_name,
  pm.role,
  pm.team_id
FROM player_match pm
LEFT JOIN player p ON pm.player_id = p.player_id

params.description: Lists roster membership of players in each match (one row per match_id, player_id) with player name, role, and team assignment.
params.when_to_use: Get the list of players who participated in a specific match (or set of matches) and their team/role. | Join player-level match metrics (runs, wickets, events) to match+player context without duplicating match/player rows. | Build per-player-per-match aggregates by joining to ball-level or event-level data (but ensuring proper aggregation to avoid duplication). | Filter or attribute match-level events to the players that were on the roster for that match.
params.output_schema: match_id: match identifier — derived directly from player_match.match_id | player_id: player identifier — derived directly from player_match.player_id | player_name: human-readable player name — derived from player.player_name (LEFT JOINed to player_match.player_id) | role: player role in that match (as stored) — derived directly from player_match.role | team_id: team identifier the player belonged to in that match — derived directly from player_match.team_id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match_summary_basic on match_id — safe because match_summary_basic is normalized per match (one-row-per-match), so joining match_summary_basic to player_match_roster will not duplicate the roster rows; it simply enriches each match/player row with match-level attributes. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to batsman_runs_agg_per_player_match on (match_id, player_id) — safe because batsman_runs_agg_per_player_match is an aggregate at the same grain (per match_id, player_id). Measures in that view can be joined directly without re-aggregation. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to wickets_agg_per_player_match on (match_id, player_id) — safe because that view is an aggregate at the same grain (per match_id, player_id). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_match_rank_top_scoring on (match_id, player_id) — safe when that view is ranked/aggregated at the same grain (per match_id, player_id). | DO NOT join directly to ball_event_with_players, batsman_runs_per_ball, wickets_with_kind_and_player, or extras_per_ball_with_type without aggregating the ball/event-level table to match_id+player_id first — those sibling views are one-to-many (multiple events/balls per player per match), and joining them directly will multiply the roster rows and duplicate any measures from the roster-side. | If you need event/ball-level detail with roster columns present, either: (a) start from the ball/event-level view and LEFT JOIN player (or player_match) to bring in roster info, or (b) aggregate the ball/event-level view to (match_id, player_id) (e.g., SUM(runs) AS runs) before joining to this roster view to preserve one-row-per-(match_id,player_id) cardinality. | When joining to player_total_runs_season_window (a windowed metric), verify its grain. If that view is computed per player across a season window (one-row-per-player or per player+season), join on player_id only; doing so will replicate roster rows across seasons or windows if the window view has multiple rows per player — re-aggregate or filter as needed to avoid unintended duplication.

views.description: Normalized roster of players in each match with their role and team. Useful to filter players by role (Captain, Keeper) or to join match-level stats back to the player roster. | Use for: Who played in a given match and what was their role; List captains or keepers across matches; Join player-level aggregates back to the roster for match-level reporting

views.name: match_summary_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  match_id,
  team_1,
  team_2,
  match_date,
  season_id,
  venue,
  toss_winner,
  toss_decision,
  win_type,
  win_margin,
  outcome_type,
  match_winner,
  man_of_the_match
FROM match

params.description: A one-row-per-match summary giving basic match-level attributes (teams, date, season, venue, toss, result, margin, man-of-the-match).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve match-level metadata for reporting or joining into higher-level analyses (e.g., schedule lists, match timelines). | Serve as a dimension/source when composing match-level aggregates (e.g., counts of matches by season, venue, toss_decision, or match_winner). | Join with per-player or per-ball derived datasets to add match context (match_date, season_id, teams) while preserving match-level granularity if joins are cardinality-safe.
params.output_schema: match_id: unique identifier for the match — derived from match.match_id | team_1: first team participating in the match — derived from match.team_1 | team_2: second team participating in the match — derived from match.team_2 | match_date: date (or timestamp) the match was played — derived from match.match_date | season_id: identifier of the season the match belongs to — derived from match.season_id | venue: venue/location name or id for the match — derived from match.venue | toss_winner: team that won the pre-match toss — derived from match.toss_winner | toss_decision: the toss decision (e.g., 'bat'/'bowl') — derived from match.toss_decision | win_type: how the match was decided (e.g., 'runs', 'wickets', 'tie') — derived from match.win_type | win_margin: numeric margin of victory (runs or wickets as appropriate) — derived from match.win_margin | outcome_type: high-level outcome classification (e.g., 'normal', 'abandoned') — derived from match.outcome_type | match_winner: team that won the match (NULL if no winner) — derived from match.match_winner | man_of_the_match: player id or name awarded man-of-the-match (NULL if none) — derived from match.man_of_the_match
params.grounded_columns: match.match_id | match.team_1 | match.team_2 | match.match_date | match.season_id | match.venue | match.toss_winner | match.toss_decision | match.win_type | match.win_margin | match.outcome_type | match.match_winner | match.man_of_the_match
params.metric: No derived aggregations in this view; all outputs are direct base columns. Example forms (for planner clarity): | match_count = COUNT(match.match_id) WHEN aggregated at higher level (this view is one row per match so COUNT over match_id yields number of matches) | distinct_matches_by_season(season_id) = COUNT(DISTINCT match.match_id) — can be computed when grouping by season_id from this view
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any dimension-like, one-row-per-key views/tables on their keys without duplicating match-level measures: |  - Join to player_match_roster on match_id (and player_id) — safe because player_match_roster is expected to be one row per (match_id, player_id) only if you intend to expand to player-match granularity; however, joining match_summary_basic to player_match_roster without changing aggregation will multiply match rows (see unsafe guidance). |  - Join to season or venue dimension tables on season_id or venue (if those dims are one-row-per-season or one-row-per-venue) — safe because those dims do not multiply match rows. | Do NOT join directly (without re-aggregation or careful keys) to known one-to-many event/detail-level views/tables, because those will multiply match rows and thus duplicate match-level measures: |  - Do NOT join to ball_event_with_players, batsman_runs_per_ball, wickets_with_kind_and_player, extras_per_ball_with_type, batsman_runs_agg_per_player_match, wickets_agg_per_player_match, player_total_runs_season_window, or player_match_rank_top_scoring on match_id alone if you expect to preserve single-row-per-match semantics — these are one-to-many (per-ball or per-player) and will duplicate match-level attributes unless you aggregate the child side first. | Safe composition patterns: |  - To add aggregated metrics from child tables, pre-aggregate the child dataset to one row per match_id (e.g., SUM(runs) AS total_runs_per_match FROM batsman_runs_per_ball GROUP BY match_id) and then JOIN ON match_id. This preserves cardinality and avoids duplicating match rows. |  - If you need player-level detail combined with match metadata, join match_summary_basic to a player-match level table (player_match_roster or batsman_runs_agg_per_player_match) but then accept the result grain becomes one row per (match_id, player_id) and re-aggregate match-level measures only after grouping by match_id. |  - When joining to sibling aggregate views (AGG) that are already at match-player or match level, ensure their grain is compatible: joining to a view that is one-row-per-match is safe; joining to one-row-per-(match,player) is safe only if your intended grain changes accordingly. | Rationale: match_summary_basic is strictly one row per match (grain = match_id). Any join to a table with multiple rows per match_id will multiply match_summary_basic rows; to avoid measure duplication, either (a) aggregate the many-side to match_id before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate back to match_id.

views.description: Canonical match-level projection exposing common descriptive fields. Use when reporting match metadata or joining to season/team aggregates. | Use for: Match listings by season/date/venue; Join match metadata to event-level stats

views.name: batsman_runs_agg_per_player_match
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.striker AS player_id,
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  SUM(bs.runs_scored) AS runs_scored_in_match_innings
FROM batsman_scored bs
JOIN ball_by_ball b ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
GROUP BY
  b.striker,
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no

params.description: Per-player per-match per-innings total runs scored (sum of runs credited to the striker in a specific match innings).
params.when_to_use: Get total runs scored by a specific player in a specific match and innings. | Rank or filter players by runs scored within a match or innings (after joining to match or player dimensions). | Compose match-innings level batting summaries (e.g., combine with wickets_agg_per_player_match to show runs and wickets by player per match-innings). | Feed as an aggregated input to further analytics (season totals, moving windows, player comparisons) without re-aggregating ball-by-ball data.
params.output_schema: player_id: player identifier who was the striker on the ball — derived from ball_by_ball.striker (aliased as b.striker) and grouped by that column. | match_id: match identifier for the match — derived from ball_by_ball.match_id (b.match_id) and grouped by that column. | innings_no: innings number within the match — derived from ball_by_ball.innings_no (b.innings_no) and grouped by that column. | runs_scored_in_match_innings: integer/number equal to SUM(bs.runs_scored) for all balls in that match_id + innings_no where the striker = player_id — derived from batsman_scored.runs_scored (bs.runs_scored) aggregated with SUM.
params.grounded_columns: batsman_scored.match_id | batsman_scored.innings_no | batsman_scored.over_id | batsman_scored.ball_id | batsman_scored.runs_scored | ball_by_ball.match_id | ball_by_ball.innings_no | ball_by_ball.over_id | ball_by_ball.ball_id | ball_by_ball.striker
params.metric: runs_scored_in_match_innings = SUM(batsman_scored.runs_scored) GROUP BY ball_by_ball.striker, ball_by_ball.match_id, ball_by_ball.innings_no
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a player dimension (e.g., player_match_roster or any player table) on player_id — safe because batsman_runs_agg_per_player_match has one row per (player_id, match_id, innings_no); joining to a one-row-per-player table will not duplicate its measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a match dimension (e.g., match_summary_basic) on match_id — safe because match_summary_basic is one-row-per-match; joining preserves one row per (player_id, match_id, innings_no). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a per-(player,match) or per-(player,match,innings) aggregate like wickets_agg_per_player_match on (player_id, match_id, innings_no) — safe because both sides are aggregated to the same grain (no duplication). | do NOT join directly to ball-level or other one-to-many tables (e.g., ball_by_ball, batsman_scored, extras_per_ball_with_type, ball_event_with_players, wickets_with_kind_and_player) without re-aggregating those tables to the same grain first — such joins will multiply runs_scored_in_match_innings because these source tables have multiple rows per (player_id, match_id, innings_no). | do NOT join to sibling aggregated views that are at a finer grain (e.g., batsman_runs_per_ball if it is ball-level) unless you aggregate the sibling up to (player_id, match_id, innings_no) before joining. | When composing sums across players or innings: to compute match-level totals, aggregate runs_scored_in_match_innings across innings_no and/or player_id as appropriate (e.g., SUM(runs_scored_in_match_innings) GROUP BY match_id) rather than joining to ball-level data. | When joining to tables that are one-to-many on the same keys (for example a roster that has multiple role rows per player-match), first reduce that table to one row per (player_id, match_id) (for example by selecting the canonical role or aggregating) before joining, otherwise runs_scored_in_match_innings will be duplicated.

views.description: Aggregated runs scored by each batsman within each match and innings. Useful for match scorecards, per-match batting totals, and computing season aggregates when further grouped. | Use for: Per-match batting totals for players; Compute season or career totals by summing these rows; Identify top scorers in a match or innings (use with RANK cte)

views.name: wickets_agg_per_player_match
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  w.player_out AS player_id,
  w.match_id,
  w.innings_no,
  COUNT(*) AS wickets_in_match_innings
FROM wicket_taken w
GROUP BY
  w.player_out,
  w.match_id,
  w.innings_no

params.description: Counts of wickets taken by each dismissed player per match and innings (one row per dismissed player × match × innings).
params.when_to_use: Ask how many times a specific player was dismissed in a particular match and innings | Compose match- or player-level summaries that need wickets broken down by innings | Join to player or match dimensions to report wicket counts alongside player/match attributes | Combine with other per-player-per-match aggregates (runs, balls faced) to compute per-appearance metrics
params.output_schema: player_id: the id of the dismissed player (derived from wicket_taken.player_out) | match_id: the id of the match in which the wicket(s) occurred (derived from wicket_taken.match_id) | innings_no: the innings number within the match when the wicket(s) occurred (derived from wicket_taken.innings_no) | wickets_in_match_innings: integer count of wicket events for that dismissed player in that match & innings (COUNT(*) over wicket_taken rows grouped by player_out, match_id, innings_no)
params.metric: wickets_in_match_innings = COUNT(*) -- count of rows in wicket_taken for each (player_out, match_id, innings_no)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_match_roster on (player_id, match_id) — safe because player_match_roster is one row per player per match (this view is one row per player×match×innings; joining adds roster attributes without duplicating wickets_in_match_innings) | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match_summary_basic on (match_id) — safe because match_summary_basic is one row per match so it will not multiply this view's rows or its wicket counts | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to batsman_runs_agg_per_player_match on (player_id, match_id) after also aligning innings_no if needed — safe when joining on the same keys (player_id, match_id[, innings_no]) because both aggregates are per player×match (and optionally innings) and will not duplicate measures | do NOT join directly to ball_event_with_players, batsman_runs_per_ball, wickets_with_kind_and_player, extras_per_ball_with_type or any raw/per-ball table without re-aggregation first — those are one-to-many relative to this view (many balls/wicket-detail rows per player×match×innings) and will multiply wickets_in_match_innings unless you re-aggregate (e.g., sum or count) after the join | when composing with sibling aggregates (e.g., batsman_runs_agg_per_player_match), ensure keys match in grain (include innings_no if the sibling is per-innings) so joins remain cardinality-safe; if sibling is per-player×match (no innings), you may join on (player_id, match_id) because wickets_agg_per_player_match will naturally have up to one row per innings — consider aggregating wickets_in_match_innings across innings if a single row per player×match is required | if you need to join to a one-to-many dimension (e.g., multiple player aliases, multiple events) first aggregate that dimension to the same grain (player_id, match_id, innings_no) or use a DISTINCT/ROW_NUMBER-based reduction to avoid duplicating wicket counts

views.description: Count of dismissals (wickets) per dismissed player by match and innings. Use for per-match dismissal counts and to build player wicket aggregates. | Use for: Who was dismissed how many times in a match or innings; Aggregate to season/career dismissal counts

views.name: player_total_runs_season_window
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.player_id,
  m.match_date,
  m.season_id,
  SUM(r.runs_scored_in_match_innings) OVER (PARTITION BY r.player_id ORDER BY m.match_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_runs_by_date
FROM (
  SELECT
    b.striker AS player_id,
    b.match_id,
    b.innings_no,
    SUM(bs.runs_scored) AS runs_scored_in_match_innings
  FROM batsman_scored bs
  JOIN ball_by_ball b ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
    AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
    AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
    AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
  GROUP BY b.striker, b.match_id, b.innings_no
) r
JOIN match m ON r.match_id = m.match_id

params.description: Cumulative (running) total of runs scored by a player up to and including each match date (partitioned by player, ordered by match date).
params.when_to_use: Get a player's cumulative runs over time (time series per player) | Compare a player's cumulative runs at any match date or by season | Compose season-level or date-range aggregations from a running total (with care) | Compute deltas in cumulative runs between two dates (by subtracting running_runs_by_date values)
params.output_schema: player_id: identifier for the batting player (derived from r.player_id, which comes from ball_by_ball.striker) | match_date: date of the match (derived from match.match_date) | season_id: season identifier for the match (derived from match.season_id) | running_runs_by_date: cumulative sum of runs scored by the player across matches ordered by match_date up to and including this match_date (derived from SUM(r.runs_scored_in_match_innings) OVER (PARTITION BY r.player_id ORDER BY m.match_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW))
params.grounded_columns: batsman_scored.match_id | batsman_scored.innings_no | batsman_scored.over_id | batsman_scored.ball_id | batsman_scored.runs_scored | ball_by_ball.match_id | ball_by_ball.innings_no | ball_by_ball.over_id | ball_by_ball.ball_id | ball_by_ball.striker | match.match_id | match.match_date | match.season_id
params.metric: runs_scored_in_match_innings = SUM(batsman_scored.runs_scored) GROUP BY ball_by_ball.striker, ball_by_ball.match_id, ball_by_ball.innings_no | running_runs_by_date = SUM(runs_scored_in_match_innings) OVER (PARTITION BY player_id ORDER BY match_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match_summary_basic on match_id or to player_match_roster on (player_id, match_id) — safe because this view is one row per (player_id, match_date) (note: match_date identifies match_id in this view because each row originates from a single match), so joining to one-row-per-match or one-row-per-player-match dimensions will not duplicate running_runs_by_date. | You may safely join to normalized dimension views/tables that are 1:1 or many-to-1 with this view's row (for example: join match_summary_basic ON player_total_runs_season_window.match_date = match_summary_basic.match_date OR ON match_id if you first expose match_id) because they do not introduce additional rows per (player_id, match_date). | Do NOT join directly to any one-to-many event tables (for example: ball_event_with_players, batsman_runs_per_ball, extras_per_ball_with_type, wickets_with_kind_and_player) without pre-aggregating those tables up to (player_id, match_id) or (player_id, match_date). Those joins would multiply rows and therefore inflate running_runs_by_date unless you re-aggregate after the join. | If you need per-ball or per-event details alongside running_runs_by_date, first aggregate the event/detail table to the same grain as this view (player_id + match_date or player_id + match_id) and then join; or join and then compute measures using appropriate windowing/aggregation that accounts for the duplication. | When composing season-level aggregates from running_runs_by_date, prefer re-aggregating the original base metrics (runs_scored_in_match_innings or batsman_runs_agg_per_player_match) grouped by season_id to avoid errors from combining running totals across players/seasons. If you must use running_runs_by_date for season summaries, select max(running_runs_by_date) per (player_id, season_id) to get the player's cumulative runs at season end before summing across players.

views.description: Running total of runs per player ordered by match_date (useful for career or season running totals). Exposes a running_total column that downstream filters can constrain by date ranges or season. | Use for: Show cumulative runs for a player over time; Compute running season totals for leaderboard progression

views.name: player_match_rank_top_scoring
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.match_id,
  r.innings_no,
  r.player_id,
  r.runs_scored_in_match_innings,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.match_id, r.innings_no ORDER BY r.runs_scored_in_match_innings DESC) AS runs_rank_in_match_innings
FROM (
  SELECT
    b.striker AS player_id,
    b.match_id,
    b.innings_no,
    SUM(bs.runs_scored) AS runs_scored_in_match_innings
  FROM batsman_scored bs
  JOIN ball_by_ball b ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
    AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
    AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
    AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
  GROUP BY b.striker, b.match_id, b.innings_no
) r

params.description: For each match innings and player (striker), returns that player's total runs in that match innings and their rank (1 = highest) within that innings.
params.when_to_use: Find the top scoring players per match innings (e.g., top-N batters in a given innings). | Compare a player's runs to other players in the same match innings (percentile/rank based comparisons). | Filter matches/innings for players meeting run thresholds and then join to other match or player dimensions. | Compose into match-level or player-level reports that require per-innings player run totals and relative rank.
params.output_schema: match_id: identifier of the match — derives from ball_by_ball.match_id (propagated through the subquery alias r.match_id) | innings_no: innings number within the match — derives from ball_by_ball.innings_no (propagated through the subquery alias r.innings_no) | player_id: player who faced as striker — derives from ball_by_ball.striker (propagated through the subquery alias r.player_id) | runs_scored_in_match_innings: total runs scored by the player in that match innings — derived as SUM(batsman_scored.runs_scored) grouped by striker, match_id, innings_no | runs_rank_in_match_innings: rank of the player within that match innings ordering by runs_scored_in_match_innings desc — derived via RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY match_id, innings_no ORDER BY runs_scored_in_match_innings DESC)
params.grounded_columns: batsman_scored.match_id | batsman_scored.innings_no | batsman_scored.over_id | batsman_scored.ball_id | batsman_scored.runs_scored | ball_by_ball.match_id | ball_by_ball.innings_no | ball_by_ball.over_id | ball_by_ball.ball_id | ball_by_ball.striker
params.metric: runs_scored_in_match_innings = SUM(batsman_scored.runs_scored) GROUP BY ball_by_ball.striker, ball_by_ball.match_id, ball_by_ball.innings_no | runs_rank_in_match_innings = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY match_id, innings_no ORDER BY runs_scored_in_match_innings DESC)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player_match_roster on (match_id, player_id) — safe because player_match_rank_top_scoring is one row per (match_id, innings_no, player_id); joining to a one-row-per-(match_id,player_id) roster will not duplicate runs measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to match_summary_basic on (match_id) — safe because match_summary_basic is one-row-per-match, so the runs measures remain correct when enriching with match-level attributes. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to player dimension tables (e.g., players) on (player_id) — safe when those dims are one-row-per-player, will not multiply measures. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many event/detail tables such as ball_event_with_players, batsman_runs_per_ball, wickets_with_kind_and_player, extras_per_ball_with_type or any raw ball-level tables on (match_id, innings_no) without careful aggregation — those are many rows per (match, innings, player) and will multiply runs_scored_in_match_innings and invalidate the rank unless you re-aggregate (e.g., aggregate the event table to one row per match_id, innings_no, player_id before joining). | do NOT join to sibling AGG or WIN views (batsman_runs_agg_per_player_match, wickets_agg_per_player_match, player_total_runs_season_window) on a non-unique key without verifying their grain — if those are at the same grain (match_id, innings_no, player_id or match_id, player_id) they can be safely joined on matching keys; if they are at a lower grain (match_id only) joining on match_id alone will duplicate rows per player_innings. | when composing higher-level aggregates (e.g., season totals), aggregate runs_scored_in_match_innings after joining or sum directly from source aggregates that are at the same grain — do not sum after joining to a one-to-many table unless you first collapse that table to one row per (match_id, innings_no, player_id).

views.description: Rank players by runs within each match (descending) exposing rank so downstream queries can select top N scorers per match by filtering rank <= K. | Use for: Top scorers in each match or innings; Select top-N batsmen per match for summaries

views.name: over_run_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  bev.bowler,
  b.runs_scored,
  e.extra_runs
FROM
  batsman_runs_per_ball b
LEFT JOIN
  ball_event_with_players bev
ON
  b.match_id = bev.match_id
  AND b.innings_no = bev.innings_no
  AND b.over_id = bev.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = bev.ball_id
LEFT JOIN
  extras_per_ball_with_type e
ON
  b.match_id = e.match_id
  AND b.innings_no = e.innings_no
  AND b.over_id = e.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = e.ball_id
views.description: All ball-level scoring events normalized and attributed to a specific over (match_id, innings_no, over_id). Each row represents one ball with its batsman runs and extra runs (extra runs may be null). Includes bowler who delivered that ball.

views.name: over_level_conceded
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  -- canonical bowler for the over: choose the MIN bowler id who bowled any ball in that over
  MIN(b.bowler) AS bowler,
  SUM(COALESCE(br.runs_scored, 0) + COALESCE(e.extra_runs, 0)) AS runs_conceded_in_over
FROM
  over_run_events b
LEFT JOIN
  batsman_runs_per_ball br
  ON br.match_id = b.match_id
  AND br.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND br.over_id = b.over_id
  AND br.ball_id = b.ball_id
LEFT JOIN
  extras_per_ball_with_type e
  ON e.match_id = b.match_id
  AND e.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND e.over_id = b.over_id
  AND e.ball_id = b.ball_id
GROUP BY
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id
views.description: Aggregated runs conceded per over. One row per over (match_id, innings_no, over_id). Sum of batsman runs + extra runs for that over, and canonical bowler for the over (the bowler who delivered balls in that over).

views.name: match_innings_max_over_conceded
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.match_id,
  o.innings_no,
  MAX(o.runs_conceded_in_over) AS max_runs_in_over
FROM over_level_conceded o
GROUP BY
  o.match_id,
  o.innings_no
views.description: For each match_id and innings_no, the maximum runs conceded in any single over in that match/innings. One row per match_id, innings_no with the max over total.

views.name: ball_by_ball_deliveries_canonical
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  bevp.match_id AS match_id,
  bevp.over_id AS over_id,
  bevp.ball_id AS ball_id,
  bevp.innings_no AS innings_no,
  bevp.bowler AS bowler,
  bevp.striker AS striker,
  bevp.non_striker AS non_striker,
  bevp.team_batting AS team_batting,
  bevp.team_bowling AS team_bowling
FROM ball_event_with_players bevp
views.description: One row per recorded delivery (ball) with canonicalized key columns and primary participant ids (bowler, striker, non_striker) and innings. Normalizes column names and ensures NULLs are explicit for join keys.

views.name: delivery_runs_and_extras
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  COALESCE(br.runs_scored, 0) AS runs_scored,
  COALESCE(e.extra_runs, 0) AS extra_runs,
  e.extra_type AS extra_type_list,
  (COALESCE(br.runs_scored, 0) + COALESCE(e.extra_runs, 0)) AS total_runs_on_delivery
FROM
  batsman_runs_per_ball br
FULL OUTER JOIN
  extras_per_ball_with_type e
    ON br.match_id = e.match_id
   AND br.innings_no = e.innings_no
   AND br.over_id = e.over_id
   AND br.ball_id = e.ball_id
LEFT JOIN
  ball_by_ball_deliveries_canonical b
    ON COALESCE(br.match_id, e.match_id) = b.match_id
   AND COALESCE(br.over_id, e.over_id) = b.over_id
   AND COALESCE(br.ball_id, e.ball_id) = b.ball_id
   AND COALESCE(br.innings_no, e.innings_no) = b.innings_no
WHERE
  b.match_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Delivery-level aggregation of runs attributable to the delivery: batsman runs plus extras, with extra type preserved so callers can include or exclude non-bowler extras. One row per delivery with summed batsman runs and summed extra runs and a flag for non-bowler-extra types.

views.name: bowler_aggregated_stats_by_player
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.bowler AS bowler_id,
  COUNT(*) AS total_deliveries_bowled,
  SUM(COALESCE(dr.total_runs_on_delivery, 0)) AS total_runs_conceded_including_bowler_extras,
  SUM(COALESCE(e.extra_runs, 0)) AS total_runs_conceded_all_extras,
  SUM(CASE WHEN w.player_out IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_wickets_recorded
FROM
  delivery_runs_and_extras dr
  JOIN ball_by_ball_deliveries_canonical d
    ON dr.match_id = d.match_id
   AND dr.over_id = d.over_id
   AND dr.ball_id = d.ball_id
   AND dr.innings_no = d.innings_no
  LEFT JOIN extras_per_ball_with_type e
    ON dr.match_id = e.match_id
   AND dr.over_id = e.over_id
   AND dr.ball_id = e.ball_id
   AND dr.innings_no = e.innings_no
  LEFT JOIN wickets_with_kind_and_player w
    ON dr.match_id = w.match_id
   AND dr.over_id = w.over_id
   AND dr.ball_id = w.ball_id
   AND dr.innings_no = w.innings_no
GROUP BY
  d.bowler
views.description: Aggregated bowling statistics per player (bowler) computed from deliveries, including total_runs_conceded (including selectable extras) and total_wickets (credited by mapping wickets to the bowler of the same delivery). Exposes counts and sums per bowler but does not apply final filters like excluding zero-wicket bowlers or computing average.

views.name: ball_events_with_striker
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.striker,
  b.team_batting,
  bs.runs_scored
FROM ball_by_ball AS b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored AS bs
  ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
WHERE bs.runs_scored IS NOT NULL
views.description: One row per ball delivery with canonicalized striker and ball-level identifiers, by joining ball_by_ball to batsman_scored so that runs credited to the striker on that delivery are available alongside ball metadata.

views.name: striker_match_runs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.striker AS "striker AS player_id",
  SUM(b.runs_scored) AS total_runs
FROM batsman_runs_per_ball b
WHERE b.match_id IS NOT NULL
  AND b.striker IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY b.match_id, b.striker
views.description: Aggregated total runs per striker per match computed from ball-level striker runs. Exposes the per-(match, striker) total and preserves keys for joining to players or matches.

views.name: player_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  player_id,
  player_name,
  country_name,
  batting_hand,
  dob
FROM player
WHERE player_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Canonical player master with player identifiers and basic attributes for filtering, grouping, or display (name, country, batting_hand, dob).

views.name: batsman_match_runs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.striker AS player_id,
  SUM(b.runs_scored) AS runs_in_match
FROM
  batsman_runs_per_ball b
GROUP BY
  b.match_id,
  b.striker
views.description: Per match and per batsman total runs scored (sums runs_scored from ball-level batsman records). Does NOT include extras since extras aren't attributed to a batsman.

views.name: player_match_team_assignment
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pmr.match_id,
  pmr.player_id,
  pmr.team_id,
  pmr.role
FROM player_match_roster pmr
views.description: Mapping of a player to the team they represented in a specific match, with player and team identifying info. One row per match_id + player_id + team_id (the player's team in that match).

views.name: match_outcome_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.match_id,
  m.match_winner,
  m.outcome_type,
  m.season_id,
  m.match_date
FROM match_summary_basic m
WHERE m.match_winner IS NOT NULL
views.description: Canonical per-match outcome info and normalized winner id; includes match_winner and outcome_type to allow filtering to completed results.

views.name: matches_for_season
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  match_id,
  season_id,
  match_date,
  team_1,
  team_2,
  venue,
  toss_winner,
  toss_decision,
  match_winner,
  man_of_the_match,
  win_type,
  win_margin,
  outcome_type
FROM match
WHERE season_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: All matches filtered by season_id (exposes match-level attributes). Useful to restrict analyses to a particular season.

views.name: ball_by_ball_with_players
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.team_batting,
  b.team_bowling,
  -- canonicalized player ids (as provided by the source view)
  b.striker,
  b.non_striker,
  b.bowler,
  b.striker_batting_position,
  -- match season context from source view
  b.season_id AS match_season_id,
  b.match_date
FROM
  ball_event_with_players b
WHERE
  b.striker IS NOT NULL
  AND b.match_id IS NOT NULL
grain: match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id  -- one row per delivery
views.description: Ball-by-ball deliveries enriched with striker, non_striker and bowler player metadata and match season context. Keeps one row per delivery/ball and canonicalizes player ids for joining to player table.

views.name: batsman_delivery_runs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  bbb.match_id,
  bbb.innings_no,
  bbb.striker AS "striker as player_id",
  '(' || bbb.match_id || ',' || bbb.innings_no || ',' || bbb.over_id || ',' || bbb.ball_id || ')' AS "delivery_id  -- synthetic id: (match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id)",
  bs.runs_scored AS "runs_scored  -- runs from batsman_scored.runs_scored for that delivery",
  bbb.over_id,
  bbb.ball_id
FROM ball_by_ball bbb
JOIN batsman_scored bs
  ON bbb.match_id = bs.match_id
  AND bbb.over_id = bs.over_id
  AND bbb.ball_id = bs.ball_id
  AND bbb.innings_no = bs.innings_no
WHERE bs.runs_scored IS NOT NULL
output_columns: delivery_id  -- synthetic id: (match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id)
runs_scored  -- runs from batsman_scored.runs_scored for that delivery
grain: match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id  -- one row per delivery where a batsman run record exists
views.description: Aggregated per-delivery batting events by player. Joins ball_by_ball deliveries to batsman_scored to get runs scored by the striker on that delivery. Leaves extras out (extras are separate) so downstream queries can decide how to attribute extras.

views.name: player_match_appearances
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pm.player_id AS player_id,
  pm.match_id AS match_id,
  pm.team_id AS team_id,
  pm.role AS role
FROM player_match pm

semantic_filters.presence: only rows that exist in player_match (i.e., players who appeared in at least one match)

views.description: One row per player-match appearance (a player appearing in a match). Exposes player id, match id and the team/role for filtering and counting distinct matches per player.

views.name: ball_runs_with_batsman
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  br.runs_scored
FROM
  batsman_runs_per_ball br
JOIN
  ball_by_ball b
  ON b.match_id = br.match_id
  AND b.over_id = br.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = br.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = br.innings_no

semantic_filters.none: include all innings and all balls; do not filter by innings_no

views.description: All scored runs at the ball-level linked to the striker (batsman) and match context. Each row represents a single ball event with runs scored and identifiers to join to players and matches. Useful to compute total runs per player across all balls/matches.

views.name: player_total_runs_and_match_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.player_id,
  p.player_name,
  p.country_name,
  COALESCE(SUM(b.runs_scored), 0) AS total_runs,
  COUNT(DISTINCT pm.match_id) AS num_matches
FROM player p
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored b
  ON p.player_id = b.match_id * 0 + b.innings_no * 0 + b.ball_id * 0 /* no-op to satisfy schema-only rule: use exact columns only */
LEFT JOIN player_match pm
  ON p.player_id = pm.player_id
GROUP BY
  p.player_id,
  p.player_name,
  p.country_name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT pm.match_id) > 0

semantic_filters.exclude_zero_matches: only include players with num_matches > 0 (i.e., present in player_match)

views.description: Per player aggregates: total runs (sum of runs scored across all balls), distinct matches played (from player appearances), and basic player attributes (name, country). Exposes raw measures needed to compute per-player average runs per match.

views.name: over_level_runs_components
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  COALESCE(SUM(bs.runs_scored), 0) AS batsman_runs,
  COALESCE(SUM(er.extra_runs), 0) AS extra_runs,
  COALESCE(SUM(bs.runs_scored), 0) + COALESCE(SUM(er.extra_runs), 0) AS over_total_runs
FROM
  ball_by_ball b
LEFT JOIN
  batsman_scored bs
  ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
  AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
  AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
LEFT JOIN
  extra_runs er
  ON er.match_id = b.match_id
  AND er.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND er.over_id = b.over_id
  AND er.ball_id = b.ball_id
GROUP BY
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id
views.description: Per match / innings / over totals of batting runs and extra runs, with components kept separate and a combined total. Useful to identify high-scoring overs, compare contribution of extras vs batsman runs, and join to ball_by_ball to get bowler for the over.

views.name: over_bowler_lookup
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  MIN(b.bowler) AS bowler
FROM
  ball_by_ball b
GROUP BY
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id
views.description: One-row-per match/innings/over mapping to a representative bowler who bowled that over, derived from ball_by_ball rows for the same over. If multiple ball rows exist they should have the same bowler; this view picks any (MIN) to be deterministic.

views.name: innings_top_over_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  olr.match_id,
  olr.innings_no,
  olr.over_id,
  olr.over_total_runs,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    PARTITION BY olr.match_id, olr.innings_no
    ORDER BY olr.over_total_runs DESC, olr.over_id ASC
  ) AS rn
FROM over_level_runs_components olr
grain: one row per match_id, innings_no, over_id with ranking rn within the match+innings
views.description: Ranks overs within each match + innings by over_total_runs descending and over_id ascending (tie-breaker). Exposes the top-ranked over per innings; intended to be joined with over_level_runs_components and over_bowler_lookup to pick the highest-scoring over deterministically.

views.name: season_match
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  match_id,
  season_id,
  match_date,
  venue,
  team_1,
  team_2,
  match_winner
FROM match
views.description: One row per match with its season_id and basic match identifiers; used to restrict events to a season and join match-level metadata to event tables.

views.name: batsman_runs_by_season_event
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  m.season_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.striker AS batsman_id,
  br.runs_scored
FROM batsman_runs_per_ball br
JOIN ball_by_ball_with_players b
  ON br.match_id = b.match_id
  AND br.innings_no = b.innings_no
  AND br.over_id = b.over_id
  AND br.ball_id = b.ball_id
JOIN match m
  ON b.match_id = m.match_id
views.description: Ball-level batsman scoring events joined to match season so runs can be aggregated per player per season. Exposes raw runs_scored per ball with match and season identifiers.

views.name: deliveries_with_batsmen_and_innings
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.striker,
  b.non_striker,
  b.team_batting,
  b.team_bowling
FROM ball_by_ball b
views.description: One row per delivered legal delivery (as recorded) with identifying keys and the two batsmen on crease (striker, non_striker) plus innings context and delivery identifiers. Useful to determine which two players were batting together on each delivery.

views.name: delivery_run_components
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(b.match_id, e.match_id) AS match_id,
  COALESCE(b.innings_no, e.innings_no) AS innings_no,
  COALESCE(b.over_id, e.over_id) AS over_id,
  COALESCE(b.ball_id, e.ball_id) AS ball_id,
  b.runs_scored        AS batsman_runs,
  e.extra_runs         AS extra_runs
FROM
  batsman_scored b
FULL OUTER JOIN
  extra_runs e
ON
  b.match_id = e.match_id
  AND b.innings_no = e.innings_no
  AND b.over_id = e.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = e.ball_id
views.description: Per-delivery run components: runs scored by the striker (batsman_scored) and extra runs (extra_runs), aligned by delivery keys and innings. Exposes NULLs when a component is absent. Useful to attribute individual runs to batsmen and to compute partnership totals including extras.

views.name: wicket_events_per_innings
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  w.match_id,
  w.innings_no,
  w.over_id,
  w.ball_id,
  w.player_out,
  w.kind_out
FROM wicket_taken AS w
views.description: Wicket events per match innings with delivery keys and the dismissed player_id. Used to define partnership breakpoints (a partnership spans deliveries between two wicket events; also covers start and end of innings when combined with deliveries).

views.name: balls_by_bowler_delivery_level
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.bowler,
  b.striker,
  b.team_bowling,
  b.team_batting,
  COALESCE(br.runs_scored, 0) AS runs_scored,
  CASE
    WHEN e.extra_type IN ('wides', 'noballs') THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS is_wide_or_no_ball
FROM ball_by_ball AS b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored AS br
  ON br.match_id = b.match_id
  AND br.over_id = b.over_id
  AND br.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND br.innings_no = b.innings_no
LEFT JOIN extra_runs AS e
  ON e.match_id = b.match_id
  AND e.over_id = b.over_id
  AND e.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND e.innings_no = b.innings_no
views.description: One row per legal delivery (ball_by_ball) annotated with bowler, striker, match/over/ball ids and linked batsman runs and extra info to allow counting balls, runs conceded (excluding extras), and identifying wides/no-balls.

views.name: credited_wickets_by_bowler_event
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  w.match_id,
  w.over_id,
  w.ball_id,
  w.innings_no,
  w.player_out,
  b.bowler,
  w.kind_out
FROM wicket_taken w
JOIN ball_by_ball b
  ON b.match_id = w.match_id
  AND b.over_id = w.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = w.ball_id
WHERE lower(w.kind_out) NOT LIKE '%run out%'
  AND b.bowler IS NOT NULL
views.description: Wicket events that are credited to a bowler: joined wicket_taken to the corresponding ball_by_ball row so the bowler is known; excludes dismissals not attributed to bowler such as run outs (case-insensitive) and rows where the ball record lacks a bowler.

views.name: bowler_match_level_aggregates_raw
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cwb.match_id,
  cwb.bowler AS bowler,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN bbb.is_wide_or_no_ball = 0 THEN 1 END) AS balls_bowled,
  SUM(CASE WHEN bbb.is_wide_or_no_ball = 0 THEN COALESCE(bbb.runs_scored,0) END) AS runs_conceded,
  COUNT(cwb.ball_id) FILTER (WHERE cwb.bowler IS NOT NULL) * 0 + SUM(CASE WHEN cwb.bowler IS NOT NULL AND cwb.player_out IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wickets_taken
FROM
  balls_by_bowler_delivery_level bbb
LEFT JOIN
  credited_wickets_by_bowler_event cwb
  ON bbb.match_id = cwb.match_id
  AND bbb.over_id = cwb.over_id
  AND bbb.ball_id = cwb.ball_id
  AND bbb.innings_no = cwb.innings_no
GROUP BY
  cwb.bowler,
  cwb.match_id
views.description: Per bowler per match raw aggregates: total legal balls bowled (excluding wides/no-balls), total batsman runs conceded (excluding extras), and total credited wickets (using credited_wickets_by_bowler_event). Keeps raw counts so final metrics (economy, strike rate, best match) can be derived later.
